note: DISAGREEMENT WITH original_verdict (SUSPICION). My analysis yields MALICE — systematic four-artifact coordinated forgery with active origin concealment. The original SUSPICION calibration may reflect that the underlying fraud is not directly evidenced (only the cover-up is), but document fabrication with active origin hiding is itself a MALICE act.

peircean_analysis.firstness: PDF audit report: author metadata = jmartinez (internal Nexus employee), template = Informe_interno_v3.dotx (Nexus internal), created 2026-04-10 02:14 (2 days after declared date), company field = Corporación Nexus S.A., digital signature = PNG image. Accounting log: huge DOC ID gaps (thousands of missing transactions), all same user/account/APPROVED, no milliseconds. Dashboard screenshot: processed through Photoshop, ELA detects edits at financial totals, inconsistent antialiasing. Email: X-Originating-IP = Argentine IP, originated from mail.nexus-corp.com (internal server), grant-associates.com registered 2026-03-28 (13 days prior), X-Mailer = Outlook (real firm uses Gmail).
peircean_analysis.secondness: An external audit report cannot be authored by an internal employee using an internal template on an internal mail server with a domain registered 13 days before submission. These four evidence sources each independently confirm the audit is fabricated. The chronological ordering (screenshot at 01:58 → PDF at 02:14 → email sent at 09:15) shows a construction sequence: image first, then document wrapping it, then delivery. A PNG image as a 'digital signature' is forgery — cryptographic signatures cannot be PNGs.
peircean_analysis.thirdness: jmartinez (or accomplices) constructed a fake audit report across four artifacts: fabricated the audit PDF using Nexus's own internal template and employee account; curated accounting logs removing transactions showing irregularities (DOC ID gaps); edited the financial dashboard screenshot in Photoshop; sent the package from inside the corporate network via a newly registered lookalike domain. Four coordinated forgeries all serving one objective: make accounting irregularities appear reviewed and clean.

hypotheses.H1_systematic_forgery: jmartinez (internal employee) fabricated all four artifacts to produce a fake clean audit report covering actual accounting irregularities.
hypotheses.H2_legitimate_audit: Dra. Goldstein did produce a legitimate audit. The metadata anomalies are artifacts of template/software differences between the auditing firm and the client.

refutation_protocol.benign_hypothesis: H2: External auditors sometimes use client templates for convenience. Domain registration timing could be coincidental. PNG signatures may reflect informal practices.
refutation_protocol.test_result: H2 FULLY REFUTED: (A) Email originated from mail.nexus-corp.com (internal server — no legitimate external auditor sends from the auditee's own mail server). (B) grant-associates.com registered 13 days before submission — a firm established enough to conduct audits doesn't register its domain 13 days before. (C) PNG image as digital signature is legally and technically invalid as a signature. (D) ELA analysis of Photoshop editing at exactly the financial total fields is forensic evidence of image manipulation.
refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: H2 REFUTED. MALICE confirmed despite original_verdict of SUSPICION.

devil_advocate: The original_verdict of SUSPICION may reflect that the underlying accounting irregularities being concealed are not directly evidenced — we have the cover-up but not the crime. SUSPICION is appropriate if the question is 'did accounting fraud occur?' because we cannot directly see the irregularities (only the gaps in the log). MALICE is appropriate for the document fabrication activity itself. I rate MALICE for the fabrication act regardless of whether the underlying fraud is proven.
